programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha ’ad uile trang a’ deànamh na rudan air a bheil iad math, ach Beag Chlangair a-mhàin - chan eil coltas ro thrang aireasan. Tha Beag air cuir roimhe rudeigin air a bheil e math a dhèanamh cuideachd. Everyone is busy doing what they’re good at except for Beag Chlangai, he doesn’t appear to be too busy. Beag has also decided he would like to try to do something he’s good at.

programme.title: Losgannan | Froglets
programme.desc: Cuiridh Ailig suas teanta agus thèid na Losgannan don fhàsach a rannsachadh phioramaidean. When Alex sets up a tent, the Froglets head into the desert as ancient pyramid explorers.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha Oona 's May ag argamaid, 's an dithis aca den bheachd gur iad as luaithe. Tha iad a cur romhpa rèis an aghaidh a chèile son co-dhùnadh a dhèanamh ach chan e Oona neo May a tha buannachadh aig deireadh an là ach farpaiseach mi-choltach! Oona and May get into an argument, both believing that they are faster than the other. They decide to race one another to see who is right, but they both end up being beaten by an unlikely competitor.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Tha droch stoirm ag adhbharachadh bùrach uabhasach. Tha Oona 's Baba a cuideachadh le bhith sgioblachadh nuair a chi iad g' eil an t-s ide air Silky fhàgail àrd am measg nan creagan, gun dòigh faighinn air ais dhan fhairge 's gu teaghlach. A wild storm leaves puffin rock in a bit of a mess. As Oona and Baba prepare to help clean it up, they discover that the weather and high tides have left Silky stranded on the cliff with no way back to sea and her family.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc: Sreath ùr anns a bheil Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann òga agus a’ faighinn a-mach ciamar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluiche cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Florence agus a gearra-mhucan. ‘S e Buttercup is Bluebell na h-ainmean a th’ orra agus tha iad beag agus bòidheach. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh gearra-mhucan agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Florence, Buttercup is Bluebell a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean. Eilidh visits Florence and her gorgeous guinea pigs, Buttercup and Bluebell. We find out how to look after guinea pigs and all the lovely stuff Florence, Buttercup and Bluebell get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on how best to handle, train and feed pets.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: Tha na h-Abadas air bothan a dhèanamh anns an taigh agus a' faighinn tòrr spòrs bho bhith cluich anns an uisge. Tha facal an là-an-diugh co-cheangailte ri cumail tioram, cuideachd. Dè th'ann agus càite an lorg iad e? The Abadas have made a den inside the house and are having a lot of fun playing in the rain. Today's word has something to do with keeping dry, too. What could it be and where will they find it?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Catriona Nic a’ Phì a’ leughadh Edie. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Sophy Henn agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Catriona MacPhee reads Edie, written and illustrated by Sophy Henn and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair nach eil fear a’ ghiotàr 'son cluich as a' chòmhlan aig Mìcheal aig seotha tàlant na sgoil’, tha Stella a' gabhail àit'. An dùil am bi i soirbheachail? When the guitar player doesn’t want to play in Mìcheal’s band at the school talent show, Stella takes his place. Will she be successful?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royals Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella ’son na Bànrigh a chuideachadh. Tha i airson gum bi i a’ dèanamh rudeigin àbhaisteach, mar gum bi i na ball den Chlub Leabhair. Ach, dè cho àbhaisteach sa tha e nuair a tha a’ Bhànrigh a' dol ann? Stella wants to help the Queen. She wants her to do something normal, like becoming a member of the Book Club. But how normal is it when the Queen attends?

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Tha Lan na sgìthear saor-stoidhleach ach feumaidh e ròghnachadh an e cur-seachad proifeiseanta a th’ ann neo nach e. 'S e amas am bliadhna an co-fharpais nàiseanta a bhuannachadh. Lan is a free-style skier but he must decide if he wants it to be a professional pastime or not. His ambition this year is to win the national competition.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha sìth eadar Sebastian is Camshron cudromach an-diugh gus am fàs Gabriel nas fheàrr – agus gus am faigh iad mathanas bhuaithe cuideachd! Peace is very important between Sebastian and Cameron today so that Gabriel gets better - and earn his forgiveness also!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Nuair a lorgas an tuathanach gu bheil pìoban ag aoidion, tha e a' cur fios air a' Bhòrd Uisge. Ach fiùs am measg nan duilgheadasan a tha seo, tha an treud a' faicinn cothrom airson beagan fealla-dha! When the farmer discovers he's sprung a leak, he calls the water board to come and fix the problem. The bored flock are thrilled by the opportunity to have some watery fun. When the workmen clock off, the party begins!

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc: Cumaidh Bircher Muesli a’ dol thu fad na maidne, agus air a stòradh sa frids, faodar a chumail airson latha no dhà! A Bircher muesli will keep you going all morning, and by being stored in the fridge it will stretch for a few days! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap set on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: An Cuan Sgith (The Minch)
programme.desc: Anne Lundon goes in search of stories and people connected to the famous stretch of sea, known as The Minch. From the west coast mainland of Scotland to the easterly coast of the Hebrides, Anne discovers how the rich culture of our coastal waters are always evolving, and kept alive by those who live beside them. Tha Anne Lundon a’ sireadh sgeulachdan agus daoine ceangailte ris a mhuir ainmeil, a’ Chuain Sgìth – bhon chost an iar tìr-mòr na h-Alba, gu costa sear Innse Gall. Tha Anne a lorg mur a tha beartas nan cladaichean againn ag atharrachadh, s’air an cumail beo leis an sluagh tha fuireach ri’n taobh. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts a quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams winning are the Pretenders, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Seumas and Mairi or Ceit and Eilidh, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Seumas & Mairi no Ceit & Eilidh, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr? In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Valtos | Aig a’ Mhullach
programme.desc: Ceòl dannsa aig mullach a’ Chùirn Ghuirm, le na DJs Gàidhealach Valtos a’ toirt an cuid chiùil gu ìre eile le seata ciùil slàn, High Water Mark. Ceòl gun sgur bhon ùrlar-dannsaidh as àirde ann an Alba. Thig cuide ri Martyn, Dan agus Euan is iad a’ dèanamh ùrlar-dannsaidh à Stèisean Tàrmagain. Le ceòl bho Bicep, Charles J, Le Boom, Mylo, Oliver Heldens am measg eile, is cuideachd, Valtos fhèin. Dance floor fillers on top of Cairngorms as Highland DJs Valtos present High Water Mark, taking their music to new heights. In a pure, uninterrupted DJ set, join Martyn, Dan and Euan as they transform the iconic Ptarmigan Station into the highest dance floor in Scotland. Featuring tracks from Bicep, Charles J, Le Boom, Mylo and Oliver Heldens, as well as Valtos. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Runrig - The Last Dance
programme.desc: 50,000 neach-leantainn a’ dèanamh air Sruighlea gus ciurm-ciùil slàn Runrig 2018 fhaicinn, a’ comharrachadh deireadh cùrsa-beatha soirbheachail 45-bliadhna. 50,000 fans descend on Stirling to watch much-loved Scottish rock band Runrig’s 2018 poignant farewell concert, marking the end of a successful 45-year career.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Wainwright Walks
programme.desc: Julia Bradbury faces the ultimate Wainwright challenge of Scafell Pike. England's highest peak marks the climax of Julia's journey to explore the work, passion and the legacy of Alfred Wainwright, a man who has inspired millions with his illustrated guides to the Lake District. Before tackling the 3,000ft ascent, Julia seeks advice from celebrated fell runner and local sheep farmer, Jos Naylor. Then it's just a case of getting herself and her film crew to the roof of England before darkness falls.

programme.title: Operation Mincemeat
programme.desc: For more than 60 years, the real story behind Operation Mincemeat has been shrouded in secrecy. Now, Ben Macintyre reveals the extraordinary truth in a documentary based on his best-selling book. In 1943, British intelligence hatched a daring plan. As the Allies prepared to invade Sicily, their purpose was to convince the Germans that Greece was the real target. The plot to fool the Fuhrer was the brainchild of Ian Fleming, the creator of James Bond. British agents procured the body of a tramp and reinvented his entire identity. He was given a new name, an officer rank and a briefcase containing plans for a fake invasion of Greece. The body was floated off the Spanish coast where Nazi spies would find it. The deception was an astonishing success. Hitler fell for it totally, ordering his armies to Greece to await an invasion that never happened. Meanwhile, the Allies landed in Sicily with minimal resistance. The island fell in a month. The war turned in the Allies' favour. Together with original witnesses, Macintyre recreates the remarkable story of how one brilliant team, and one dead tramp, pulled off a deception which changed the course of history.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson examines the remains of a lost harbour in Port Carlisle, Cumbria, a small village near Carlisle which grew as a consequence of the canal building surge that swept the nation. For a very short time, this village was a thriving port with ambitions to rival Liverpool. It welcomed tourists, but its canal was soon overtaken by the advent of the railways. Ben goes on to discover the cauldron-like original boiler behind the Victorian bath house.

programme.desc: Fresh from his surprise appearance during the World Cup Final half-time show, Gustavo Dudamel leads the Los Angeles Philharmonic in its first Proms appearance for more than two decades. programme.title: Top of the Pops

programme.title: Ultimate Cover Versions at the BBC
programme.desc: Smash hits from 60 years of great cover versions in performance from the BBC TV archive. Reinterpretations, tributes and acts of subversion from the British invasion to noughties X Factor finalist Alexandra Burke. Artists as varied as The Moody Blues, Soft Cell, Mariah Carey and UB40 with their 'retake' on someone else's song - ultimate chart hits that are, in some cases, perhaps even better than the original. Arguably The Beatles, alongside Bob Dylan and The Beach Boys, introduced the notion of 'originality' and self-generating artists writing their songs into the pop lexicon in the 60s. One of the most fascinating consequences of this has been the 'original' cover version, a reinterpretation of someone else's song that has transformed it into pop gold with a shift of rhythm, intent and context. The pop cover has proved a remarkably imaginative and durable form and this compilation tracks this pop alchemy at its finest and most intriguing.

programme.title: Ultimate Cover Versions at the BBC
programme.desc: It’s time for a return trip through the best of the BBC’s music archives, celebrating more of the songs that are so good, other artists haven’t be able to resist recording their own versions. This extravaganza features the best in pop, rock and soul from the past five decades and features artists ranging from Adele and Annie Lennox to Happy Mondays and Manic Street Preachers.

programme.title: Operation Mincemeat
programme.desc: For more than 60 years, the real story behind Operation Mincemeat has been shrouded in secrecy. Now, Ben Macintyre reveals the extraordinary truth in a documentary based on his best-selling book. In 1943, British intelligence hatched a daring plan. As the Allies prepared to invade Sicily, their purpose was to convince the Germans that Greece was the real target. The plot to fool the Fuhrer was the brainchild of Ian Fleming, the creator of James Bond. British agents procured the body of a tramp and reinvented his entire identity. He was given a new name, an officer rank and a briefcase containing plans for a fake invasion of Greece. The body was floated off the Spanish coast where Nazi spies would find it. The deception was an astonishing success. Hitler fell for it totally, ordering his armies to Greece to await an invasion that never happened. Meanwhile, the Allies landed in Sicily with minimal resistance. The island fell in a month. The war turned in the Allies' favour. Together with original witnesses, Macintyre recreates the remarkable story of how one brilliant team, and one dead tramp, pulled off a deception which changed the course of history.

programme.title: Villages by the Sea
programme.desc: Ben Robinson examines the remains of a lost harbour in Port Carlisle, Cumbria, a small village near Carlisle which grew as a consequence of the canal building surge that swept the nation. For a very short time, this village was a thriving port with ambitions to rival Liverpool. It welcomed tourists, but its canal was soon overtaken by the advent of the railways. Ben goes on to discover the cauldron-like original boiler behind the Victorian bath house.

programme.desc: Fresh from his surprise appearance during the World Cup Final half-time show, Gustavo Dudamel leads the Los Angeles Philharmonic in its first Proms appearance for more than two decades. Beethoven's electrifying Seventh Symphony, hailed by Wagner as 'the apotheosis of the dance', is paired with Gabriela Ortiz's powerful Revolucion diamantina, a gripping score inspired by Mexico's 2019 'glitter revolution' that pulses with hypnotic rhythms and defiant energy.

programme.title: Ultimate Cover Versions at the BBC
programme.desc: Smash hits from 60 years of great cover versions in performance from the BBC TV archive. Reinterpretations, tributes and acts of subversion from the British invasion to noughties X Factor finalist Alexandra Burke. Artists as varied as The Moody Blues, Soft Cell, Mariah Carey and UB40 with their 'retake' on someone else's song - ultimate chart hits that are, in some cases, perhaps even better than the original. Arguably The Beatles, alongside Bob Dylan and The Beach Boys, introduced the notion of 'originality' and self-generating artists writing their songs into the pop lexicon in the 60s. One of the most fascinating consequences of this has been the 'original' cover version, a reinterpretation of someone else's song that has transformed it into pop gold with a shift of rhythm, intent and context. The pop cover has proved a remarkably imaginative and durable form and this compilation tracks this pop alchemy at its finest and most intriguing.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night for Keely Hodgkinson as she goes for gold in the final of the women’s 800m on day 5 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The defending champion will face tough competition from the fastest woman in the world this year, Switzerland’s Audrey Werro. Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Alan Carr's Picture Slam
programme.desc: Comedian Alan Carr returns to host the fun and frantic quiz show where every question is a picture and every picture is worth cash. They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Samantha and Shane from Coventry, siblings Taran and Raj from London and father and son Adam and Oliver from Glasgow. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: It’s a race against time to unify a pride of lions before they turn on one of the females. Can old boys Klaus and Simba save the day? And Megan McCubbin encourages a native to return to the woods.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: It’s destination Argyll and Bute today. Sonali Shah tours this region of Scotland in search of a new home for a couple from a Warwickshire town who have a budget of £340,000. Sonali almost takes to the water on Loch Lomond, as she lends a hand to help a group of volunteers restoring the last paddle steamer to be built in Britain, a treasured relic of Scottish history.

programme.title: The One Show
programme.desc: An extended 20th-anniversary special sees Alex Jones and Roman Kemp bring together some of the biggest names, favourite stories and standout moments from the show. Joined by the wider family of presenters, they look back at the inspiring stories that have shaped the programme, from its Children in Need fundraising legacy to the impact it has had on viewers. Plus a special music performance to mark the occasion.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night for Keely Hodgkinson as she goes for gold in the final of the women’s 800m on day 5 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The defending champion will face tough competition from the fastest woman in the world this year, Switzerland’s Audrey Werro. Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night for Keely Hodgkinson as she goes for gold in the final of the women’s 800m on day 5 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The defending champion will face tough competition from the fastest woman in the world this year, Switzerland’s Audrey Werro. Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: It’s a race against time to unify a pride of lions before they turn on one of the females. Can old boys Klaus and Simba save the day? And Megan McCubbin encourages a native to return to the woods.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

They could be anything from famous faces, places, products or logos, and teams need to name them all for a Picture Slam. Playing this time are friends Samantha and Shane from Coventry, siblings Taran and Raj from London and father and son Adam and Oliver from Glasgow. They battle it out across four rounds, shouting out answers and building their banks. But only one team can make it to the final Super Slam for the chance to win £10,000.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night for Keely Hodgkinson as she goes for gold in the final of the women’s 800m on day 5 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The defending champion will face tough competition from the fastest woman in the world this year, Switzerland’s Audrey Werro. Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: It’s a huge night for Keely Hodgkinson as she goes for gold in the final of the women’s 800m on day 5 of the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham. The defending champion will face tough competition from the fastest woman in the world this year, Switzerland’s Audrey Werro. Five other gold medals are up for grabs: the women’s 10,000m, the men’s high jump, the women’s discus, the men’s 200m and the men's 400m hurdles, which has Karsten Warholm going for his fourth European title. Gabby Logan leads the coverage from the studio alongside Jessica Ennis-Hill and Greg Rutherford, with Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe in commentary.

programme.title: Animal Park
programme.desc: It’s a race against time to unify a pride of lions before they turn on one of the females. Can old boys Klaus and Simba save the day? And Megan McCubbin encourages a native to return to the woods.

programme.title: Trace, Track, Get My Car Back
programme.desc: Tracker Richard is on the hunt for an unusual item that’s been snatched from a building site. It’s a specialised shower unit used by construction workers who have been exposed to hazardous substances, and without it, work has come to a halt. The vehicle’s tracker leads Richard, and the police, to a location in the West Country. Will they get it back without retaliation from the ruthless thieves? Organised crime gangs often target luxury supercars due to their high value on the black market. And the thieves will stop at nothing to get their hands on them – even arming themselves with weapons. When motor sports enthusiast Mark Cowne viewed CCTV footage of his Ferrari Pista being stolen, he was shocked to see the machete-wielding crooks in action. But a specialist vehicle-tracking company is on a mission to get it back. It's not just cars the criminals set their sights on. Valuable electric bikes are also being stolen in cities across the UK. In London, bike recovery specialist Bilal is on the hunt for an e-bike, and the GPS signal has led him to a property in a block of flats. But when the resident gives him access, he’s shocked to discover what appears to be a bike chop shop.

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The women’s heptathlon kick-starts the morning session on day five of the European Athletics Championships, featuring world bronze medallist Katarina Johnson-Thompson. World silver medallist Jake Wightman is the one to watch in qualifying for the men’s 1,500m. And all eyes will be on men’s pole vault qualifying as Mondo Duplantis seeks his fourth European title in a row. Jeanette Kwakye is joined in the studio by Jessica Ennis-Hill, Greg Rutherford and Jenny Meadows. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.desc: Shaun escapes through a ‘portal’ inside Shirley’s wool to flee an annoying Bitzer, only to emerge into a chaotic version of the farm without him. Desperate to escape, he repeatedly jumps back inside Shirley, emerging somewhere worse each time!

programme.title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
programme.desc: High school student Miles is catapulted into conflict when he gets powers like his hero Spider-Man. A device accessing parallel universes goes dangerously wrong but drags some surprising Spidey-related allies into his world. Lively, stylish animated adventure.

programme.title: Death in Paradise
programme.desc: Mervin begrudgingly embraces island life and agrees to watch a local women’s football game with the team. But half-time sees a bloody discovery when the star player is found dead in the locker rooms with a fatal bullet wound. The team are left perplexed when it becomes clear that the only way to access the changing rooms is via the pitch - and no-one in the crowd saw anything. So, how did the killer slip through the net? As Mervin feels the pressure from Selwyn over a murder that took place right under their noses, Naomi is at a crossroads when someone from her past turns up on the island.

programme.title: Ghosts Australia
programme.desc: The Australian version of the hit UK series. When city couple Kate and Sean inherit Ramshead Manor, a run-down country estate, they see it as a sign for a fresh new start. But after Kate has a near-death experience, she gains the ability to see and hear ghosts – and discovers there are several living in the mansion. Kate must navigate the ghosts' issues while trying to start a hotel business with Sean, who remains unable to see them.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: Barbara is a fashion influencer who posts about #girlpower all day long but is too busy hustling to attend a protest. Elise is an awkward English exchange student who’s come to Australia to reinvent herself as a one-woman Pussy Riot but is a bit too scared of getting in trouble. After a chance meeting in art class, and fed up with the boyfriends and professors in their lives, the two girls decide to take a stand. In the dead of night and drunk as skunks, they deface the University Quadrangle, spray-painting it with the words ‘Kill All Men’. The next morning they wake to news that the university’s star rugby player has been murdered, castrated, and plonked on top of their political statement with those very same words carved into his chest. Sure, Elise and Barbara could tell the cops about their co-opted political statement, but the terms of Elise’s scholarship stipulate ‘no misconduct’, and Barbara’s extensive list of Insta endorsement deals rests on her being strictly apolitical. So now it’s up to the girls to erase their ties to the crime, and track down the real culprit. Simple, right? They wish. Bad feminists. Worse detectives.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: Two days after the shocking murder, the police detain a suspect, and the vice-chancellor pleads for the students to remain calm. Barbara receives an anonymous threat, but that’s not all. The police are looking for evidence, whilst Elise and Barbara try to conceal any on them on the night of the murder. The girls must work out a way to destroy the evidence before the police can get it while having enough time to meet their anonymous antagonist and also keeping up their usual appearances of campus queen and eccentric exchange student.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: With a second murder victim found on campus, University Club Day proves the perfect place for Elise and Barbara to search for the killer. Unfortunately, Shepherd and Roach have the exact same idea. Meanwhile, the vice-chancellor employs a self-defence coach for vulnerable male students.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: With Prue behaving strangely in front of Elise, the girls must crash a feminist protest party to find out what she remembers about the night of the murders. Meanwhile, Shepherd is philosophically torn as the vice-chancellor demands she shut the entire protest party down.

programme.title: He Had It Coming
programme.desc: As Elise and Barbara's friendship strains, Elise finds solace with university improv theatre legend Kaye Blanchett. The only problem is Kaye is just a little bit connected to every single murder.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Girls Aloud or Little Mix? The 1970s or the 1980s? Summer Olympics or Winter Olympics? As today’s teams battle it out, every answer is a 50/50 shot on The Answer Run.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: With three items saved from Witley Recycling Centre in Surrey, upcycling expert Sarah Moore gets to work trying to turn trash into cash. For her own project, Sarah tries to make the sun shine a profit on a garden umbrella. and a pair of tired 70s armchairs puts upholsterer Larissa through her paces.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: There is one beautiful thing that the British and the French have in common, and that’s the pride taken in local dishes. But can the French persuade Marcus that there’s a local lamb dish to rival his beloved Lancashire hotpot? Marcus’s time in Saint-Remy is nearly at an end, and if there's one thing he’s learnt, it's when it comes to food, keep it simple. Now, he’s been invited to a local farm party, but the catch is he has to bring a dish - so he needs inspiration for a celebratory but simple recipe to say farewell to all the friends he’s made in Provence.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: The south Wales valleys are the setting of the final outing for best pals Margie Cooper and Tim Medhurst. They head towards Cardiff in their electric-powered former fire engine. Hitting the shops, our pair summon the support of the spirits with a pottery obelisk and some spooky psychic sketches. We learn a secret 19th-century language as one antique fan finds an antique, um, fan. In Brynmawr, Margie finds out about the life and attire of legendary wrestler Adrian Street, while Tim steps into the ring and learns not to grapple with the Welsh the hard way. At their final auction 'slam-down', will it be Tim or Margie who ends up on the mat?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui is in Westcliff-on-Sea in Essex to look at a two-bedroom maisonette bought by a mother-and-son developing team. Martin is in Coleford, Gloucestershire, near the Forest of Dean, to see a flat in real need of renovation. And Dion is just south of Stoke-on-Trent in Barlaston to see a three-bedroom end-of-terrace bought to become a new family home.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Danny Sebastian makes sure both teams are on the right track on today’s episode from Oswestry Showground. Roo Irvine is guiding the red team, siblings Chris and Sally. Their opponents in blue are self-confessed ‘drama queens’ Valerie and Wanda, skippered by Colin Young. The blues spot a giant set of scales, and Colin volunteers to weigh himself – but it’s the price that turns out to be hefty! Meanwhile, Sally sniffs out a possible deal on an incense jar, but Roo doubts it will make a profit at auction. Near Oswestry, Danny visits a unique collection of monorails at a light railway, including one that appeared in a villain’s lair in a James Bond movie! Over the border in Wales, auctioneer Matthew Tong is on the rostrum, doing his best to help the teams make a profit. Who will be going home with money in their pockets?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts the final day of the week’s whistlestop tour of the UK. EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, are this week’s players, and this is their final chance to claim glory. As ever, Paul Gorton is the unreliable tour guide, and he’s taking the players to Wrexham.

programme.title: The Great Rift: Africa's Wild Heart
programme.desc: Visible from space, Africa's Great Rift Valley runs three thousand miles from the Red Sea to the mouth of the Zambezi. It's a diverse terrain of erupting volcanoes, forest-clad mountains, spectacular valleys, rolling grasslands, huge lakes and mighty rivers, and is home to crocodiles, hippos, lions, elephants, flocks of flamingos and a diversity of indigenous peoples. Using state-of-the-art high definition filming techniques, this series investigates the geological forces which shaped east Africa's Great Rift and which make it one of the world's most wildlife-rich landscapes. The Great Rift Valley channels a huge diversity of waterways - rivers, lakes, waterfalls, caustic springs and coral seas - from Egypt to Mozambique. Some lake and ocean deeps harbour previously unseen life-forms, while caustic waters challenge life to the extreme. But where volcanic minerals enrich the Great Rift's waterways, they provide the most spectacular concentrations of birds, mammals and fish in all Africa.

programme.title: The Great Rift: Africa's Wild Heart
programme.desc: Visible from space, Africa's Great Rift Valley runs three thousand miles from the Red Sea to the mouth of the Zambezi. It's a diverse terrain of erupting volcanoes, forest-clad mountains, spectacular valleys, rolling grasslands, huge lakes and mighty rivers, and is home to crocodiles, hippos, lions, elephants, flocks of flamingos and a diversity of indigenous peoples. Using state-of-the-art high definition filming techniques, this series investigates the geological forces which shaped east Africa's Great Rift and which make it one of the world's most wildlife-rich landscapes. The Great Rift Valley provides the stage for an epic battle between trees and grass - its course influenced by volcanic eruptions, landscape and rainfall. On its outcome rests the fate of Africa's great game herds. In the rift's savannas, grazers and their predators struggle to outwit each other, forcing one group of primates to develop a social system that paved the way for the evolution of mankind.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. At Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire finds include a collection of bronzes bought on the internet, a portrait by Stanley Spencer, and fine examples of pottery. Sir Reresby Sitwell takes a close look at what is purported to be Robin Hood's bow.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The show comes from Milestones Museum in Basingstoke, a place bursting with remnants from Basingstoke's industrial past. Elizabeth Talbot and James Lewis find the best antiques and collectibles to take to auction from the assembled crowd, while presenter Paul Martin visits the home of the man now considered to be the father of ecology, 18th-century naturalist Gilbert White.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Chris Bisson, Danielle Harold, Katharine Merry and Robert Webb take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games decanter, or will they be tempted by the House of Games retro bag?

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Married couple Steve and Jenny are in conflict over what house to buy. After a long career, Steve is preparing to leave the army, so for the first time in their relationship, the couple need to buy a property. However, they have very different ideas about what they want and need. The couple take on a raft-building challenge to highlight how they solve problems together. They must each then do a climb and make a leap of faith for a reward bag. Mediator Dave works with them to find out why they have struggled to resolve this issue so far. Is it really about the size of the mortgage, or is there more to it? At the end of two days in the wild, will only one of them be getting the house they want, or will they find a way to compromise?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The heptathlon continues on day five of the European Athletics Championships with the third event of seven, the shot put, kick-starting the evening session. Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Jade O’Dowda represent Great Britain in Birmingham, with Ireland’s Kate O’Connor another contender for gold. The women’s 10,000m also gets underway on the track, with Megan Keith part of the team after winning European bronze two years ago. Gabby Logan is alongside Jessica Ennis Hill and Greg Rutherford in the studio. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As the drought takes its toll on Longmeadow, Monty takes stock of his garden and has a radical rethink about what he should be growing in the future. With this in mind, he takes cuttings of some drought-resistant plants as a way of saving money. There is also a rambling rose in desperate need of a haircut and lots of produce to harvest in the veg garden, so as always, there is plenty to be getting on with. Frances Tophill visits the picturesque village of Clovelly in north Devon, where gardening on a clifftop is not without its challenges. And in Norfolk, Adam Frost explores a walled kitchen garden steeped in history but planted with a modern eye. On the Isle of Wight, a couple tell the incredible story of how they’ve reimagined the Victorian garden of the poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson, while a gardener in East Anglia showcases his love of naturalistic planting.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Arthur Wakefield is ready to throw Julien to the wolves, when there’s a shocking revelation about the night of Cate’s murder that changes everything. Bergerac is blown off course until he makes a major breakthrough in the search for Cate’s missing phone and he feels like he is about to close back in on his chief suspect. But with Bergerac’s behaviour becoming increasingly erratic, will he even be able to continue the investigation? Meanwhile, Arthur Wakefield is drawn to even more extreme measures to stop him.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi has fun with some ticks, a bit of tax, a few toes – and a pile of matchboxes that plays tic-tac-toe with Rose Matafeo, Lou Sanders, Ross Noble and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: On Falling
programme.desc: Portuguese immigrant Aurora is struggling to get by in a dead-end warehouse job in Scotland. Her life is severely limited - unless she can find some hope.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: CCTV raises doubts over Bethany’s honesty. Gabs turns to the Climate Front for help. A new drawing from Bethany leads Gabs and Dick to the old ruins, where the truth is revealed.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: The south Wales valleys are the setting of the final outing for best pals Margie Cooper and Tim Medhurst. They head towards Cardiff in their electric-powered former fire engine. programme.title: Bargain Hunt

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?

As ever, Paul Gorton is the unreliable tour guide, and he’s taking the players to Wrexham.

programme.title: The Great Rift: Africa's Wild Heart
programme.desc: Visible from space, Africa's Great Rift Valley runs three thousand miles from the Red Sea to the mouth of the Zambezi. It's a diverse terrain of erupting volcanoes, forest-clad mountains, spectacular valleys, rolling grasslands, huge lakes and mighty rivers, and is home to crocodiles, hippos, lions, elephants, flocks of flamingos and a diversity of indigenous peoples. Using state-of-the-art high definition filming techniques, this series investigates the geological forces which shaped east Africa's Great Rift and which make it one of the world's most wildlife-rich landscapes. The Great Rift Valley channels a huge diversity of waterways - rivers, lakes, waterfalls, caustic springs and coral seas - from Egypt to Mozambique. Some lake and ocean deeps harbour previously unseen life-forms, while caustic waters challenge life to the extreme. But where volcanic minerals enrich the Great Rift's waterways, they provide the most spectacular concentrations of birds, mammals and fish in all Africa.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow

programme.title: Flog It!

programme.title: Bear Grylls - Wild Reckoning
programme.desc: Married couple Steve and Jenny are in conflict over what house to buy. After a long career, Steve is preparing to leave the army, so for the first time in their relationship, the couple need to buy a property. However, they have very different ideas about what they want and need. The couple take on a raft-building challenge to highlight how they solve problems together. They must each then do a climb and make a leap of faith for a reward bag. Mediator Dave works with them to find out why they have struggled to resolve this issue so far. Is it really about the size of the mortgage, or is there more to it? At the end of two days in the wild, will only one of them be getting the house they want, or will they find a way to compromise?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The heptathlon continues on day five of the European Athletics Championships with the third event of seven, the shot put, kick-starting the evening session. Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Jade O’Dowda represent Great Britain in Birmingham, with Ireland’s Kate O’Connor another contender for gold. The women’s 10,000m also gets underway on the track, with Megan Keith part of the team after winning European bronze two years ago. Gabby Logan is alongside Jessica Ennis Hill and Greg Rutherford in the studio. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As the drought takes its toll on Longmeadow, Monty takes stock of his garden and has a radical rethink about what he should be growing in the future. With this in mind, he takes cuttings of some drought-resistant plants as a way of saving money. There is also a rambling rose in desperate need of a haircut and lots of produce to harvest in the veg garden, so as always, there is plenty to be getting on with. Frances Tophill visits the picturesque village of Clovelly in north Devon, where gardening on a clifftop is not without its challenges. And in Norfolk, Adam Frost explores a walled kitchen garden steeped in history but planted with a modern eye. On the Isle of Wight, a couple tell the incredible story of how they’ve reimagined the Victorian garden of the poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson, while a gardener in East Anglia showcases his love of naturalistic planting.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Arthur Wakefield is ready to throw Julien to the wolves, when there’s a shocking revelation about the night of Cate’s murder that changes everything. Bergerac is blown off course until he makes a major breakthrough in the search for Cate’s missing phone and he feels like he is about to close back in on his chief suspect. But with Bergerac’s behaviour becoming increasingly erratic, will he even be able to continue the investigation? Meanwhile, Arthur Wakefield is drawn to even more extreme measures to stop him.

After a long career, Steve is preparing to leave the army, so for the first time in their relationship, the couple need to buy a property. However, they have very different ideas about what they want and need. The couple take on a raft-building challenge to highlight how they solve problems together. They must each then do a climb and make a leap of faith for a reward bag. Mediator Dave works with them to find out why they have struggled to resolve this issue so far. Is it really about the size of the mortgage, or is there more to it? At the end of two days in the wild, will only one of them be getting the house they want, or will they find a way to compromise?

programme.title: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: The heptathlon continues on day five of the European Athletics Championships with the third event of seven, the shot put, kick-starting the evening session. Katarina Johnson-Thompson and Jade O’Dowda represent Great Britain in Birmingham, with Ireland’s Kate O’Connor another contender for gold. The women’s 10,000m also gets underway on the track, with Megan Keith part of the team after winning European bronze two years ago. Gabby Logan is alongside Jessica Ennis Hill and Greg Rutherford in the studio. Commentary comes from Steve Cram, Steve Backley, Andrew Cotter, Colin Jackson and Paula Radcliffe.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As the drought takes its toll on Longmeadow, Monty takes stock of his garden and has a radical rethink about what he should be growing in the future. With this in mind, he takes cuttings of some drought-resistant plants as a way of saving money. There is also a rambling rose in desperate need of a haircut and lots of produce to harvest in the veg garden, so as always, there is plenty to be getting on with. Frances Tophill visits the picturesque village of Clovelly in north Devon, where gardening on a clifftop is not without its challenges. And in Norfolk, Adam Frost explores a walled kitchen garden steeped in history but planted with a modern eye. On the Isle of Wight, a couple tell the incredible story of how they’ve reimagined the Victorian garden of the poet Alfred, Lord Tennyson, while a gardener in East Anglia showcases his love of naturalistic planting.

programme.title: Bergerac
programme.desc: Arthur Wakefield is ready to throw Julien to the wolves, when there’s a shocking revelation about the night of Cate’s murder that changes everything. Bergerac is blown off course until he makes a major breakthrough in the search for Cate’s missing phone and he feels like he is about to close back in on his chief suspect. But with Bergerac’s behaviour becoming increasingly erratic, will he even be able to continue the investigation? Meanwhile, Arthur Wakefield is drawn to even more extreme measures to stop him.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi has fun with some ticks, a bit of tax, a few toes – and a pile of matchboxes that plays tic-tac-toe with Rose Matafeo, Lou Sanders, Ross Noble and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Paddy O'Connell.

programme.title: On Falling
programme.desc: Portuguese immigrant Aurora is struggling to get by in a dead-end warehouse job in Scotland. Her life is severely limited - unless she can find some hope.

programme.title: The Rapture
programme.desc: CCTV raises doubts over Bethany’s honesty. Gabs turns to the Climate Front for help. A new drawing from Bethany leads Gabs and Dick to the old ruins, where the truth is revealed.

programme.title: Evolution
programme.desc: How did the dolphin get so smart? Chris Packham dives into one of the biggest questions in nature - how intelligence itself evolved and how it arose in the extraordinary mind of the dolphin. Inside each one lies the result of a three-billion-year journey, from light-sensing cells to conscious thought.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: The Answer Run
programme.desc: Girls Aloud or Little Mix? The 1970s or the 1980s? Summer Olympics or Winter Olympics? As today’s teams battle it out, every answer is a 50/50 shot on The Answer Run.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: With three items saved from Witley Recycling Centre in Surrey, upcycling expert Sarah Moore gets to work trying to turn trash into cash. For her own project, Sarah tries to make the sun shine a profit on a garden umbrella. and a pair of tired 70s armchairs puts upholsterer Larissa through her paces.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: There is one beautiful thing that the British and the French have in common, and that’s the pride taken in local dishes. But can the French persuade Marcus that there’s a local lamb dish to rival his beloved Lancashire hotpot? Marcus’s time in Saint-Remy is nearly at an end, and if there's one thing he’s learnt, it's when it comes to food, keep it simple. Now, he’s been invited to a local farm party, but the catch is he has to bring a dish - so he needs inspiration for a celebratory but simple recipe to say farewell to all the friends he’s made in Provence.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: The south Wales valleys are the setting of the final outing for best pals Margie Cooper and Tim Medhurst. They head towards Cardiff in their electric-powered former fire engine. Hitting the shops, our pair summon the support of the spirits with a pottery obelisk and some spooky psychic sketches. We learn a secret 19th-century language as one antique fan finds an antique, um, fan. In Brynmawr, Margie finds out about the life and attire of legendary wrestler Adrian Street, while Tim steps into the ring and learns not to grapple with the Welsh the hard way. At their final auction 'slam-down', will it be Tim or Margie who ends up on the mat?

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Jacqui is in Westcliff-on-Sea in Essex to look at a two-bedroom maisonette bought by a mother-and-son developing team. Martin is in Coleford, Gloucestershire, near the Forest of Dean, to see a flat in real need of renovation. And Dion is just south of Stoke-on-Trent in Barlaston to see a three-bedroom end-of-terrace bought to become a new family home.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Danny Sebastian makes sure both teams are on the right track on today’s episode from Oswestry Showground. Roo Irvine is guiding the red team, siblings Chris and Sally. Their opponents in blue are self-confessed ‘drama queens’ Valerie and Wanda, skippered by Colin Young. The blues spot a giant set of scales, and Colin volunteers to weigh himself – but it’s the price that turns out to be hefty! Meanwhile, Sally sniffs out a possible deal on an incense jar, but Roo doubts it will make a profit at auction. Near Oswestry, Danny visits a unique collection of monorails at a light railway, including one that appeared in a villain’s lair in a James Bond movie! Over the border in Wales, auctioneer Matthew Tong is on the rostrum, doing his best to help the teams make a profit. Who will be going home with money in their pockets?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Mehreen Baig, Clare Balding, Jamie Laing and Mike Wozniak take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games reusable coffee mug, which is brand new for this series?

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp and his sidekick Sarah Greene host this quiz show, where the contestants race on moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers stop them in their tracks. Five contestants battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races, where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Do You Know Your Place?
programme.desc: Vernon Kay hosts the final day of the week’s whistlestop tour of the UK. EastEnders star Nitin Ganatra, the Rev Kate Bottley and Alex Gray, aka Apollo from Gladiators, are this week’s players, and this is their final chance to claim glory. As ever, Paul Gorton is the unreliable tour guide, and he’s taking the players to Wrexham.

programme.title: The Great Rift: Africa's Wild Heart
programme.desc: Visible from space, Africa's Great Rift Valley runs three thousand miles from the Red Sea to the mouth of the Zambezi. It's a diverse terrain of erupting volcanoes, forest-clad mountains, spectacular valleys, rolling grasslands, huge lakes and mighty rivers, and is home to crocodiles, hippos, lions, elephants, flocks of flamingos and a diversity of indigenous peoples. Using state-of-the-art high definition filming techniques, this series investigates the geological forces which shaped east Africa's Great Rift and which make it one of the world's most wildlife-rich landscapes. The Great Rift Valley channels a huge diversity of waterways - rivers, lakes, waterfalls, caustic springs and coral seas - from Egypt to Mozambique. Some lake and ocean deeps harbour previously unseen life-forms, while caustic waters challenge life to the extreme. But where volcanic minerals enrich the Great Rift's waterways, they provide the most spectacular concentrations of birds, mammals and fish in all Africa.

programme.title: The Great Rift: Africa's Wild Heart
programme.desc: Visible from space, Africa's Great Rift Valley runs three thousand miles from the Red Sea to the mouth of the Zambezi. It's a diverse terrain of erupting volcanoes, forest-clad mountains, spectacular valleys, rolling grasslands, huge lakes and mighty rivers, and is home to crocodiles, hippos, lions, elephants, flocks of flamingos and a diversity of indigenous peoples. Using state-of-the-art high definition filming techniques, this series investigates the geological forces which shaped east Africa's Great Rift and which make it one of the world's most wildlife-rich landscapes. The Great Rift Valley provides the stage for an epic battle between trees and grass - its course influenced by volcanic eruptions, landscape and rainfall. On its outcome rests the fate of Africa's great game herds. In the rift's savannas, grazers and their predators struggle to outwit each other, forcing one group of primates to develop a social system that paved the way for the evolution of mankind.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination. At Renishaw Hall in Derbyshire finds include a collection of bronzes bought on the internet, a portrait by Stanley Spencer, and fine examples of pottery. Sir Reresby Sitwell takes a close look at what is purported to be Robin Hood's bow.

programme.desc: Grandmaster Glitch is out on a camping expedition in Mongolia. There's not much around except a group of Mongolian nomads - people who travel around the country with their animals, camping in amazing tents called gers. Glitch visits their camp and inadvertently offends them, then his misfiring jetpack causes him to land on one of their precious horses, causing it to gallop away from the camp with Glitch on its back! The Go Jetters take to the Vroomster to try and stop Glitch and the runaway horse but end up scaring the horses and causing a stampede. They need click-ons to calm down the Mongolian horses before things get out of control.
